---
title: "Container-based agents"
---

::: {.guide-card}
![](../assets/img/cards/containers.svg){.card-icon}

## tl;dr

Container execution gives your agents the same workflow with stronger sandboxing. Agents run inside Docker or Podman containers instead of local tmux sessions -- they cannot access your host filesystem outside the worktree, and crosslink hooks still enforce all policy automatically.
:::

&nbsp;

## Why containers?

- **Isolation** -- agents cannot access your host filesystem outside the worktree
- **Reproducibility** -- consistent environment regardless of host OS
- **Security** -- provider execution may use a broader sandbox only inside the configured external container boundary; Crosslink hooks still enforce repository policy
- **Cross-platform** -- works on Windows, Linux, and macOS anywhere Docker runs

&nbsp;

### Local sandbox alternative

If you can't run Docker or Podman but still want host isolation, set
`sandbox.command` in `hook-config.json`. The configured command wraps the
structured provider invocation at the shell boundary.

```bash
crosslink config set sandbox.command "firejail --quiet --net=none"
```

A container is still the stronger answer when one is available -- this lever just makes the local path less raw when it's the only option.

&nbsp;

---

## Quick start

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**You say / do:**

> "Run this feature agent in a container so it's fully sandboxed."

You want stronger isolation than a local tmux session. The container approach is a single flag change.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
→
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Agent executes:**

```bash
crosslink kickoff run "add batch retry logic" \
  --container docker
```

Creates branch, worktree, builds the image (if needed), starts a container, and launches the agent inside it.
:::
:::

&nbsp;

---

## Managing container lifecycle

### Getting the image

The default image used by `--container docker|podman` is published to GitHub Container Registry as
[`ghcr.io/corvidae-coding-projects/crosslink-agent`](https://github.com/Corvidae-Coding-Projects/crosslink/pkgs/container/crosslink-agent),
built for both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. Published tags:

- `:latest` — the most recent tagged release
- `:<version>` (e.g. `:0.5.2`) — pinned release
- `:nightly` — floating tag tracking `develop`
- `:nightly-<short-sha>` — immutable nightly snapshots

The first `--container docker` launch will pull the image automatically; subsequent launches reuse the local copy. Pin `--image ghcr.io/corvidae-coding-projects/crosslink-agent:<version>` for reproducible runs.

### Building the image locally

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**You say / do:**

> "Build the agent image from source instead of pulling."

Useful when iterating on `crosslink/resources/container/Dockerfile` or running offline. Produces a single-arch image tagged `:local`.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
→
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Agent executes:**

```bash
just build-image            # tags :local
crosslink kickoff run "..." \
  --container docker \
  --image ghcr.io/corvidae-coding-projects/crosslink-agent:local
```

The image includes both Claude Code and Codex CLIs, Crosslink, git, Python,
`uv`, and non-root UID remapping. The entrypoint installs both repository
integrations without changing `agent.provider` and runs the final process as
the remapped non-root user.
:::
:::

### Monitoring containers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**You say / do:**

> "What are my container agents doing?"

You can list running containers, stream logs, and open interactive shells for debugging.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
→
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Agent executes:**

```bash
crosslink container ps
crosslink container logs my-feature -f
```

Lists all running agent containers and streams live output from a specific agent.
:::
:::

### Manual control

```bash
# Start a container manually for an existing worktree
crosslink container start .worktrees/my-feature \
  --issue 42 \
  --prompt .worktrees/my-feature/KICKOFF.md

# Graceful stop
crosslink container stop my-feature

# Stop and remove
crosslink container kill my-feature

# Remove a stopped container
crosslink container rm my-feature
```

&nbsp;

## Repository hooks inside containers

The same Crosslink repository hooks used in local sessions also run inside containers:

- **Git mutations blocked** -- `git push`, `git merge`, `git rebase` are blocked by hooks
- **Commits gated** -- `git commit` requires an active crosslink issue
- **Stub detection** -- post-edit hooks catch TODOs and incomplete code
- **Session state** -- active issue and heartbeat data remain available

The rule hook remains installed in the container. Its bundled Markdown inputs are
zero bytes, matching local execution.

Container execution maps the selected provider to an externally isolated
posture. Codex may use danger-full-access only inside that boundary; host Codex
defaults to workspace-write.

Authentication uses normal interactive account login in provider- and
user-scoped persistent volumes. No API-key environment variables are accepted
or forwarded:

```bash
crosslink container auth login --provider codex
crosslink container auth status --provider codex
crosslink container auth refresh --provider claude
crosslink container auth logout --provider codex
```

&nbsp;

---

## Integration with kickoff

The `--container` flag on `crosslink kickoff run` handles the full workflow:

1. Creates a feature branch and worktree
2. Builds the container image (if not already built)
3. Starts a container with the worktree mounted
4. Launches the agent inside the container
5. The agent works autonomously: explore, implement, test, commit

```bash
# Local tmux (default)
crosslink kickoff run "my feature"

# Docker container
crosslink kickoff run "my feature" --container docker

# Podman container
crosslink kickoff run "my feature" --container podman
```
